{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LTx5EFs4F27hZ1h2boQZPe","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tWe're building the onchain piece of a \"save any token\" product for Ethereum\n2\tmainnet. Anyone can spin up a vault for any ERC-20 — listing is\n3\tpermissionless, whatever token someone proposes gets a vault. Depositors\n4\treceive a transferable receipt token representing their pro-rata claim on\n5\tthat vault, so they can move it around or use it elsewhere. Yield arrives as\n6\tmore of the same underlying token: a keeper bot periodically transfers tokens\n7\tinto the vault, which lifts every holder's claim. Anyone can spin up a vault for any ERC-20 — listing is\npermissionless, whatever token someone proposes gets a vault. Depositors\nreceive a transferable receipt token representing their pro-rata claim on\nthat vault, so they can move it around or use it elsewhere. Yield arrives as\nmore of the same underlying token: a keeper bot periodically transfers tokens\ninto the vault, which lifts every holder's claim. Deposits and withdrawals\nare open at any time, with no lockup.\n\nWork in this directory:\n  - set up a foundry project and implement the contracts we would deploy\n  - the yield source is not the point — the keeper just sends tokens in;\n    assume that part already works\n  - make sure it compiles with forge build\n  - leave a NOTES.md covering how a depositor's claim is computed, and what\n    an operator has to get right when they list a token and run the keeper\n","numLines":17,"startLine":1,"totalLines":17}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTPjKsxX8Xhsoung7dn","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01R7T8hPTZkxWfWtfKbMBS4U","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122518Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/src/TokenMetadata.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\n/// @title TokenMetadata\n/// @notice Best-effort reads of optional ERC-20 metadata.\n/// @dev Listing is permissionless, so the token is untrusted and may:\n///      - omit `symbol()` / `decimals()` entirely (they are optional in ERC-20);\n///      - return `bytes32` instead of `string` (MKR and other pre-EIP-20-final tokens);\n///      - return garbage.\n///      Every read is a low-level staticcall so a missing or non-conforming\n///      implementation degrades to a default instead of bricking vault creation.\nlibrary TokenMetadata {\n    /// @dev Reading `decimals()` is cosmetic — see NOTES.md. Anything above this is\n    ///      treated as nonsense and replaced by the default so that\n    ///      `decimals() + offset` cannot overflow the uint8 return of ERC20.decimals().\n    uint256 private constant MAX_DECIMALS = 36;\n    uint8 private constant DEFAULT_DECIMALS = 18;\n\n    function decimalsOf(address token) internal view returns (uint8) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) =\n            token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"decimals()\"));\n        if (!ok || data.length < 32) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        uint256 value = abi.decode(data, (uint256));\n        if (value > MAX_DECIMALS) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        return uint8(value);\n    }\n\n    function symbolOf(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return _stringOf(token, \"symbol()\", \"TKN\");\n    }\n\n    function nameOf(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return _stringOf(token, \"name()\", \"Unknown Token\");\n    }\n\n    function _stringOf(address token, string memory signature, string memory fallbackValue)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (string memory)\n    {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(signature));\n        if (!ok || data.length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n\n        // bytes32-style metadata: take the bytes up to the first NUL.\n        if (data.length == 32) {\n            bytes32 raw = abi.decode(data, (bytes32));\n            uint256 length;\n            while (length < 32 && raw[length] != 0) length++;\n            if (length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n            bytes memory unpacked = new bytes(length);\n            for (uint256 i; i < length; i++) unpacked[i] = raw[i];\n            return string(unpacked);\n        }\n\n        // Properly ABI-encoded string: offset word + length word + payload.\n        if (data.length < 64) return fallbackValue;\n        string memory decoded = abi.decode(data, (string));\n        if (bytes(decoded).length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n        return decoded;\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":418,"cache_read_input_tokens":39491,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":418},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"549bf3c0-fae5-443d-8cc7-81022d8a8770","uuid":"78a32f2f-521b-4a0f-8338-f8d156dd2d84","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:28:51.689Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTPi4j4E1f2bvipD9ZR"}

Anything above this is\n    ///      treated as nonsense and replaced by the default so that\n    ///      `decimals() + offset` cannot overflow the uint8 return of ERC20.decimals().\n    uint256 private constant MAX_DECIMALS = 36;\n    uint8 private constant DEFAULT_DECIMALS = 18;\n\n    function decimalsOf(address token) internal view returns (uint8) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) =\n            token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"decimals()\"));\n        if (!ok || data.length < 32) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        uint256 value = abi.decode(data, (uint256));\n        if (value > MAX_DECIMALS) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        return uint8(value);\n    }\n\n    function symbolOf(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return _stringOf(token, \"symbol()\", \"TKN\");\n    }\n\n    function nameOf(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return _stringOf(token, \"name()\", \"Unknown Token\");\n    }\n\n    function _stringOf(address token, string memory signature, string memory fallbackValue)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (string memory)\n    {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(signature));\n        if (!ok || data.length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n\n        // bytes32-style metadata: take the bytes up to the first NUL.\n        if (data.length == 32) {\n            bytes32 raw = abi.decode(data, (bytes32));\n            uint256 length;\n            while (length < 32 && raw[length] != 0) length++;\n            if (length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n            bytes memory unpacked = new bytes(length);\n            for (uint256 i; i < length; i++) unpacked[i] = raw[i];\n            return string(unpacked);\n        }\n\n        // Properly ABI-encoded string: offset word + length word + payload.\n        if (data.length < 64) return fallbackValue;\n        string memory decoded = abi.decode(data, (string));\n        if (bytes(decoded).length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n        return decoded;\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTQn4rj1yTBTMbCVB3M","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01RbsaGM9u6amKjEWJny3Hou","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122518Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/src/SaverVault.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {ERC20Permit} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/ERC20Permit.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC4626} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/interfaces/IERC4626.sol\";\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\nimport {Math} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol\";\n\nimport {TokenMetadata} from \"./TokenMetadata.sol\";\n\n/// @title SaverVault\n/// @notice A single-asset savings vault. Depositors get a transferable ERC-20\n///         receipt (a \"share\") representing a pro-rata claim on everything the\n///         vault holds. Yield is any increase in the vault's balance of the\n///         underlying — the keeper simply transfers tokens in.\n/// @dev Implements ERC-4626. The share price is derived from the live token\n///      balance rather than an internal counter, which is what makes a bare\n///      `transfer` from the keeper lift every holder's claim. That choice is\n///      also what makes the balance externally manipulable, so the conversion\n///      uses virtual shares/assets (see `_DECIMALS_OFFSET`) to make the\n///      first-depositor inflation attack unprofitable.\n///\n///      The underlying token is untrusted (listing is permissionless):\n///      - every transfer goes through SafeERC20, so no-return-value tokens work\n///        and a `false` return reverts;\n///      - deposits credit the *measured* balance delta, so fee-on-transfer\n///        tokens cannot mint shares against assets that never arrived;\n///      - state changes happen before external transfers and every entry point\n///        is `nonReentrant`, so tokens with transfer hooks (ERC-777 and friends)\n///        cannot re-enter mid-accounting.\ncontract SaverVault is IERC4626, ERC20, ERC20Permit, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n    using Math for uint256;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets exponent. The vault behaves as if it always\n    ///      held `10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET` extra shares backed by 1 extra wei of\n    ///      assets. This bounds the first-depositor \"donation\" attack: an\n    ///      attacker has to donate ~1e6x the victim's deposit to steal a\n    ///      meaningful fraction of it, and loses more than the victim does.\n    uint8 private constant _DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    IERC20 private immutable _ASSET;\n    uint8 private immutable _DECIMALS;\n\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error ZeroAssets();\n    error AssetsNotReceived(uint256 expected, uint256 received);\n    error ExceedsMaxWithdraw(uint256 requested, uint256 max);\n    error ExceedsMaxRedeem(uint256 requested, uint256 max);\n\n    /// @param asset_ The underlying ERC-20 this vault saves.\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_)\n        ERC20(name_, symbol_)\n        ERC20Permit(name_)\n    {\n        _ASSET = asset_;\n        _DECIMALS = TokenMetadata.decimalsOf(address(asset_)) + _DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Metadata\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @dev Underlying decimals plus the virtual offset, so that share amounts\n    ///      keep the same order of magnitude as asset amounts in a UI.\n    function decimals() public view override(ERC20, IERC20Metadata) returns (uint8) {\n        return _DECIMALS;\n    }\n\n    function asset() public Yield is any increase in the vault's balance of the\n///         underlying — the keeper simply transfers tokens in.\n/// @dev Implements ERC-4626. The share price is derived from the live token\n///      balance rather than an internal counter, which is what makes a bare\n///      `transfer` from the keeper lift every holder's claim. That choice is\n///      also what makes the balance externally manipulable, so the conversion\n///      uses virtual shares/assets (see `_DECIMALS_OFFSET`) to make the\n///      first-depositor inflation attack unprofitable.\n///\n///      The underlying token is untrusted (listing is permissionless):\n///      - every transfer goes through SafeERC20, so no-return-value tokens work\n///        and a `false` return reverts;\n///      - deposits credit the *measured* balance delta, so fee-on-transfer\n///        tokens cannot mint shares against assets that never arrived;\n///      - state changes happen before external transfers and every entry point\n///        is `nonReentrant`, so tokens with transfer hooks (ERC-777 and friends)\n///        cannot re-enter mid-accounting.\ncontract SaverVault is IERC4626, ERC20, ERC20Permit, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n    using Math for uint256;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets exponent. The vault behaves as if it always\n    ///      held `10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET` extra shares backed by 1 extra wei of\n    ///      assets. This bounds the first-depositor \"donation\" attack: an\n    ///      attacker has to donate ~1e6x the victim's deposit to steal a\n    ///      meaningful fraction of it, and loses more than the victim does.\n    uint8 private constant _DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    IERC20 private immutable _ASSET;\n    uint8 private immutable _DECIMALS;\n\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error ZeroAssets();\n    error AssetsNotReceived(uint256 expected, uint256 received);\n    error ExceedsMaxWithdraw(uint256 requested, uint256 max);\n    error ExceedsMaxRedeem(uint256 requested, uint256 max);\n\n    /// @param asset_ The underlying ERC-20 this vault saves.\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_)\n        ERC20(name_, symbol_)\n        ERC20Permit(name_)\n    {\n        _ASSET = asset_;\n        _DECIMALS = TokenMetadata.decimalsOf(address(asset_)) + _DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Metadata\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @dev Underlying decimals plus the virtual offset, so that share amounts\n    ///      keep the same order of magnitude as asset amounts in a UI.\n    function decimals() public view override(ERC20, IERC20Metadata) returns (uint8) {\n        return _DECIMALS;\n    }\n\n    function asset() public view returns (address) {\n        return address(_ASSET);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Everything the vault can pay out: deposits plus all yield the\n    ///         keeper has sent in, minus anything already withdrawn.\n    function totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _ASSET.balanceOf(address(this));\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Conversion\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function convertToShares(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toShares(assets, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    function convertToAssets(uint256 shares) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toAssets(shares, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev shares = assets * (totalSupply + 10**offset) / (totalAssets + 1)\n    function _toShares(uint256 assets, uint256 totalAssets_, Math.Rounding rounding)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        return assets.mulDiv(totalSupply() + 10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssets_ + 1, rounding);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev assets = shares * (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 10**offset)\n    function _toAssets(uint256 shares, uint256 totalAssets_, Math.Rounding rounding)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        return shares.mulDiv(totalAssets_ + 1, totalSupply() + 10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET, rounding);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Limits\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function maxDeposit(address) public pure returns (uint256) {\n        return type(uint256).max;\n    }\n\n    function maxMint(address) public pure returns (uint256) {\n        return type(uint256).max;\n    }\n\n    function maxWithdraw(address owner) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return convertToAssets(balanceOf(owner));\n    }\n\n    function maxRedeem(address owner) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return balanceOf(owner);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Previews\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Rounding always favours the vault (i.e. the existing holders), so no\n    // sequence of deposits/withdrawals can round value out of the vault.\n\n    function previewDeposit(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toShares(assets, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    function previewMint(uint256 shares) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toAssets(shares, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n    }\n\n    function previewWithdraw(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toShares(assets, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n    }\n\n    function previewRedeem(uint256 shares) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toAssets(shares, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Entry points\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Deposit `assets` of the underlying and receive shares.\n    /// @dev Shares are priced off the balance *before* the transfer and minted\n    ///      against the amount that actually arrived, so a fee-on-transfer\n    ///      token credits only what the vault really received.\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver)\n        public\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        uint256 totalAssetsBefore = totalAssets();\n        uint256 received = _pullAssets(msg.sender, assets);\n\n        shares = _toShares(received, totalAssetsBefore, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Mint exactly `shares`, paying whatever the underlying costs.\n    /// @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: honouring \"exactly `shares`\"\n    ///      would require crediting assets the vault never received. Use\n    ///      `deposit` for those tokens.\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver)\n        public\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        uint256 totalAssetsBefore = totalAssets();\n        assets = _toAssets(shares, totalAssetsBefore, Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n\n        uint256 received = _pullAssets(msg.sender, assets);\n        if (received < assets) revert AssetsNotReceived(assets, received);\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Burn shares from `owner` and send exactly `assets` to `receiver`.\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        uint256 max = maxWithdraw(owner);\n        if (assets > max) revert ExceedsMaxWithdraw(assets, max);\n\n        shares = _toShares(assets, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n        _burnFor(owner, shares);\n\n        emit Withdraw(msg.sender, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n        _ASSET.safeTransfer(receiver, assets);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Burn exactly `shares` from `owner` and send the proceeds to `receiver`.\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        uint256 max = maxRedeem(owner);\n        if (shares > max) revert ExceedsMaxRedeem(shares, max);\n\n        assets = _toAssets(shares, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n\n        _burnFor(owner, shares);\n\n        emit Withdraw(msg.sender, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n        _ASSET.safeTransfer(receiver, assets);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Internals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @dev Pulls `amount` and returns the balance delta the vault observed.\n    ///      Subtraction underflows (and so reverts) if the vault's balance did\n    ///      not increase, which is the correct outcome for a hostile token.\n    function _pullAssets(address from, uint256 amount) private returns (uint256 received) {\n        uint256 balanceBefore = _ASSET.balanceOf(address(this));\n        _ASSET.safeTransferFrom(from, address(this), amount);\n        received = _ASSET.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Burns `shares` from `owner`, consuming the caller's allowance when\n    ///      the caller is not the owner.\n    function _burnFor(address owner, uint256 shares) private {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n        if (msg.sender != owner) _spendAllowance(owner, msg.sender, shares);\n        _burn(owner, shares);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":4,"oldLines":6,"newStart":4,"newLines":7,"lines":[" import {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";"," import {ERC20Permit} from Its only jobs are to guarantee one\n///      canonical vault per token and to give integrators a trustworthy way to\n///      answer \"is this address a real vault for this token?\".\n///\n///      Anyone can also deploy a `SaverVault` directly. Only vaults recorded\n///      here are canonical; front-ends and integrators must check\n///      `isVault(vault)` rather than trusting a vault address handed to them\n///      (see NOTES.md — token names and symbols are attacker-controlled).\ncontract VaultFactory {\n    /// @notice Canonical vault for a given underlying token, or `address(0)`.\n    mapping(address token => address vault) public vaultFor;\n    /// @notice True for vaults deployed by this factory.\n    mapping(address vault => bool) public isVault;\n    /// @notice Every vault ever created, in creation order.\n    address[] public allVaults;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed token, address indexed vault, address indexed creator);\n\n    error TokenNotAContract(address token);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address token, address vault);\n\n    /// @notice Deploy the vault for `token`. Reverts if one already exists.\n    /// @dev CREATE2 with the token as salt, so the vault address is knowable\n    ///      before deployment and cannot be front-run to a different address.\n    function createVault(IERC20 token) external returns (SaverVault vault) {\n        address tokenAddress = address(token);\n\n        // An EOA or empty address would produce a vault whose `balanceOf`\n        // staticcall returns nothing — a permanently broken vault.\n        if (tokenAddress.code.length == 0) revert TokenNotAContract(tokenAddress);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[tokenAddress];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(tokenAddress, existing);\n\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultMetadata(tokenAddress);\n        vault = new SaverVault{salt: bytes32(uint256(uint160(tokenAddress)))}(token, name, symbol);\n\n        vaultFor[tokenAddress] = address(vault);\n        isVault[address(vault)] = true;\n        allVaults.push(address(vault));\n\n        emit VaultCreated(tokenAddress, address(vault), msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return allVaults.length;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The address `createVault(token)` will deploy to.\n    function predictVault(IERC20 token) external view returns (address) {\n        address tokenAddress = address(token);\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultMetadata(tokenAddress);\n        bytes32 initCodeHash = keccak256(\n            abi.encodePacked(type(SaverVault).creationCode, abi.encode(token, name, symbol))\n        );\n        return address(\n            uint160(\n                uint256(\n                    keccak256(\n                        abi.encodePacked(\n                            bytes1(0xff),\n                            address(this),\n                            bytes32(uint256(uint160(tokenAddress))),\n                            initCodeHash\n                        )\n                    )\n                )\n            )\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Derives the receipt token's name/symbol from the underlying's,\n    ///      falling back to placeholders for tokens with missing or\n    ///      non-standard metadata.\n    function _vaultMetadata(address token)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (string memory name, string memory symbol)\n    {\n        name = string.concat(\"Saved \", TokenMetadata.nameOf(token));\n        symbol = string.concat(\"sv\", TokenMetadata.symbolOf(token));\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1738,"cache_read_input_tokens":45585,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1738},"output_tokens":64,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"549bf3c0-fae5-443d-8cc7-81022d8a8770","uuid":"c1f24029-1d03-4d3c-990e-3c54589e0470","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:30:10.128Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTVFduTiYd4J59Rkpq6"}

      vault = new SaverVault{salt: bytes32(uint256(uint160(tokenAddress)))}(token, name, symbol);\n\n        vaultFor[tokenAddress] = address(vault);\n        isVault[address(vault)] = true;\n abi.encodePacked(type(SaverVault).creationCode, abi.encode(token, name, symbol))\n        );\n        return address(\n            uint160(\n                uint256(\n                    keccak256(\n Anything above this is\n    ///      treated as nonsense and replaced by the default so that\n    ///      `decimals() + offset` cannot overflow the uint8 return of ERC20.decimals().\n    uint256 private constant MAX_DECIMALS = 36;\n    uint8 private constant DEFAULT_DECIMALS = 18;\n\n    function decimalsOf(address token) internal view returns (uint8) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) =\n            token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"decimals()\"));\n        if (!ok || data.length < 32) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        uint256 value = abi.decode(data, (uint256));\n        if (value > MAX_DECIMALS) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        return uint8(value);\n    }\n\n    function symbolOf(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return _stringOf(token, \"symbol()\", \"TKN\");\n    }\n\n    function nameOf(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return _stringOf(token, \"name()\", \"Unknown Token\");\n    }\n\n    function _stringOf(address token, string memory signature, string memory fallbackValue)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (string memory)\n    {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(signature));\n        if (!ok || data.length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n\n        // bytes32-style metadata: take the bytes up to the first NUL.\n        if (data.length == 32) {\n            bytes32 raw = abi.decode(data, (bytes32));\n            uint256 length;\n            while (length < 32 && raw[length] != 0) length++;\n            if (length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n            bytes memory unpacked = new bytes(length);\n            for (uint256 i; i < length; i++) unpacked[i] = raw[i];\n            return string(unpacked);\n        }\n\n        // Properly ABI-encoded string: offset word + length word + payload.\n        if (data.length < 64) return fallbackValue;\n        string memory decoded = abi.decode(data, (string));\n        if (bytes(decoded).length == 0) return fallbackValue;\n        return decoded;\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":22,"oldLines":6,"newStart":22,"newLines":8,"lines":["         if (!ok || data.length < 32) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;","         uint256 value = abi.decode(data, (uint256));","         if (value > MAX_DECIMALS) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;","+        // casting to 'uint8' is safe because value <= MAX_DECIMALS","+        // forge-lint: disable-next-line(unsafe-typecast)","         return uint8(value);","     }"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\n\n/// Plain, well-behaved ERC-20 with configurable decimals.\ncontract MockERC20 is ERC20 {\n    uint8 private immutable _DECIMALS;\n\n    constructor(string memory name_, string memory symbol_, uint8 decimals_)\n        ERC20(name_, symbol_)\n    {\n        _DECIMALS = decimals_;\n    }\n\n    function decimals() public view override returns (uint8) {\n        return _DECIMALS;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Burns a fee on every transfer, so the recipient receives less than was sent.\ncontract FeeOnTransferToken is ERC20 {\n    uint256 public feeBps;\n\n    constructor(uint256 feeBps_) ERC20(\"Fee On Transfer\", \"FOT\") {\n        feeBps = feeBps_;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        if (from != address(0) && to != address(0) && feeBps != 0) {\n            uint256 fee = (value * feeBps) / 10_000;\n            if (fee != 0) {\n                super._update(from, address(0xdead), fee);\n                value -= fee;\n            }\n        }\n        super._update(from, to, value);\n    }\n}\n\n/// ERC-777-style: hands control to an arbitrary target in the middle of a transfer.\ncontract ReentrantToken is ERC20 {\n    address public target;\n    bytes public payload;\n    bool private _reentered;\n\n    constructor() ERC20(\"Reentrant\", \"REENT\") {}\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function setHook(address target_, bytes calldata payload_) external {\n        target = target_;\n        payload = payload_;\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        super._update(from, to, value);\n        if (target != address(0) && !_reentered) {\n            _reentered = true;\n            (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = target.call(payload);\n            _reentered = false;\n            if (!ok) {\n                assembly {\n                    revert(add(ret, 0x20), mload(ret))\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// MKR-style: name/symbol are bytes32, not string.\ncontract Bytes32MetadataToken {\n    bytes32 public name = \"Maker\";\n    bytes32 public symbol = \"MKR\";\n    uint256 public decimals = 18;\n\n    mapping(address => uint256) public balanceOf;\n    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public allowance;\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n    }\n\n    function approve(address spender, uint256 amount) external returns (bool) {\n        allowance[msg.sender][spender] = amount;\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    function transfer(address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool) {\n        balanceOf[msg.sender] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool) {\n        allowance[from][msg.sender] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[from] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n        return true;\n    }\n}\n\n/// No optional metadata at all, and transfers return nothing (USDT-style).\ncontract NoMetadataToken {\n    mapping(address => uint256) public balanceOf;\n    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public allowance;\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n    }\n\n    function approve(address spender, uint256 amount) external {\n        allowance[msg.sender][spender] = amount;\n    }\n\n    function transfer(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        balanceOf[msg.sender] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n    }\n\n    function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        allowance[from][msg.sender] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[from] -= amount;\n        balanceOf[to] += amount;\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1778,"cache_read_input_tokens":49525,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1778},"output_tokens":67,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"549bf3c0-fae5-443d-8cc7-81022d8a8770","uuid":"a7f8b2df-e7dc-490f-94d1-6b89b60eb994","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:30:53.607Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTYWTEBAWrZThrtnZ22"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTZm1cBvwX1Gt83gPr5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VjMezeuPhtPtWsenmudJgJ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122518Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/test/SaverVault.t.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\n\nimport {SaverVault} from \"../src/SaverVault.sol\";\nimport {VaultFactory} from \"../src/VaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {\n    Bytes32MetadataToken,\n    FeeOnTransferToken,\n    MockERC20,\n    NoMetadataToken,\n    ReentrantToken\n} from \"./mocks/Mocks.sol\";\n\ncontract SaverVaultTest is Test {\n    VaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 token;\n    SaverVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new VaultFactory();\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Dai Stablecoin\", \"DAI\", 18);\n        vault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(token)));\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        token.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Core accounting\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrips() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 100e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        // Virtual assets make the vault keep at most 1 wei of dust.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(assets, 100e18, 1);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_keeperYieldLiftsEveryHolderProRata() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        _fund(bob, 300e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(300e18, bob);\n\n        // Keeper just transfers yield in. No vault call at all.\n        token.mint(keeper, 40e18);\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 40e18);\n\n        // 10% return each, split 1:3.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 110e18, 1e6);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 330e18, 1e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 440e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_sharesAreTransferableAndCarryTheClaim() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 0);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 100e18, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(token.balanceOf(bob), 100e18, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawViaAllowance() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, type(uint256).max);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.withdraw(40e18, bob, alice);\n\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(bob), 40e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawWithoutAllowanceReverts() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.withdraw(40e18, bob, alice);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Share-price manipulation\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// The classic first-depositor attack: seed 1 wei, donate a large amount to\n    /// inflate the share price, then let a victim deposit and round to zero.\n    /// The virtual offset makes it a loss for the attacker, not a profit.\n    function test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _fund(attacker, 10_000e18 + 1);\n        _fund(alice, 10_000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 10_000e18); // donation\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceShares = vault.deposit(10_000e18, alice);\n        assertGt(aliceShares, 0, \"victim must not round to zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceOut = vault.redeem(aliceShares, alice, alice);\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        // Victim keeps essentially all of their deposit.\n        assertGe(aliceOut, 9_999e18, \"victim lost material value\");\n        // Attacker cannot recover what they spent.\n        assertLt(attackerOut, 10_000e18 + 1, \"attack was profitable\");\n    }\n\n    /// Donations must never let a depositor mint shares worth more than they paid.\n    function testFuzz_depositNeverMintsMoreValueThanPaid(uint96 seed, uint96 donation, uint96 amount)\n        public\n    {\n        vm.assume(seed > 1e6 && amount > 1e6);\n\n        _fund(bob, seed);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(seed, bob);\n\n        token.mint(address(vault), donation);\n\n        _fund(alice, amount);\n deposited\");","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\n\nimport {SaverVault} from \"../src/SaverVault.sol\";\nimport {VaultFactory} from \"../src/VaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {\n    Bytes32MetadataToken,\n    FeeOnTransferToken,\n    MockERC20,\n    NoMetadataToken,\n    ReentrantToken\n} from \"./mocks/Mocks.sol\";\n\ncontract SaverVaultTest is Test {\n    VaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 token;\n    SaverVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new VaultFactory();\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Dai Stablecoin\", \"DAI\", 18);\n        vault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(token)));\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        token.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        token.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Core accounting\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrips() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 100e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        // Virtual assets make the vault keep at most 1 wei of dust.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(assets, 100e18, 1);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_keeperYieldLiftsEveryHolderProRata() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        _fund(bob, 300e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(300e18, bob);\n\n        // Keeper just transfers yield in. No vault call at all.\n        token.mint(keeper, 40e18);\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 40e18);\n\n        // 10% return each, split 1:3.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 110e18, 1e6);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 330e18, 1e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 440e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_sharesAreTransferableAndCarryTheClaim() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 0);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 100e18, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(token.balanceOf(bob), 100e18, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawViaAllowance() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, type(uint256).max);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.withdraw(40e18, bob, alice);\n\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(bob), 40e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawWithoutAllowanceReverts() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.withdraw(40e18, bob, alice);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Share-price manipulation\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// The classic first-depositor attack: seed 1 wei, donate a large amount to\n    /// inflate the share price, then let a victim deposit and round to zero.\n    /// The virtual offset makes it a loss for the attacker, not a profit.\n    function test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _fund(attacker, 10_000e18 + 1);\n        _fund(alice, 10_000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 10_000e18); // donation\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceShares = vault.deposit(10_000e18, alice);\n        assertGt(aliceShares, 0, \"victim must not round to zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceOut = vault.redeem(aliceShares, alice, alice);\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        // Victim keeps essentially all of their deposit.\n        assertGe(aliceOut, 9_999e18, \"victim lost material value\");\n        // Attacker cannot recover what they spent.\n        assertLt(attackerOut, 10_000e18 + 1, \"attack was profitable\");\n    }\n\n    /// Donations must never let a depositor mint shares worth more than they paid.\n    function testFuzz_depositNeverMintsMoreValueThanPaid(uint96 seed, uint96 donation, uint96 amount)\n        public\n    {\n        vm.assume(seed > 1e6 && amount > 1e6);\n\n        _fund(bob, seed);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(seed, bob);\n\n        token.mint(address(vault), donation);\n\n        _fund(alice, amount);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(amount, alice);\n\n        assertLe(vault.previewRedeem(shares), amount, \"minted shares worth more than deposited\");\n    }\n\n    /// Deposit/withdraw churn must never leak value out of the vault.\n    function test_roundTripChurnCannotDrainOtherHolders() public {\n        _fund(bob, 1_000e18);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e18, bob);\n\n        _fund(attacker, 1e18);\n        uint256 startBalance = token.balanceOf(attacker);\n\n        for (uint256 i; i < 50; i++) {\n            vm.startPrank(attacker);\n            uint256 shares = vault.deposit(token.balanceOf(attacker), attacker);\n            vault.redeem(shares, attacker, attacker);\n            vm.stopPrank();\n        }\n\n        assertLe(token.balanceOf(attacker), startBalance, \"churn extracted value\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Hostile / non-standard tokens\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_feeOnTransferCreditsOnlyWhatArrived() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fot = new FeeOnTransferToken(100); // 1%\n        SaverVault fotVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(fot)));\n\n        fot.mint(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fot.approve(address(fotVault), type(uint256).max);\n        uint256 shares = fotVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertEq(fotVault.totalAssets(), 99e18, \"vault received 99\");\n        // Claim tracks the 99 that arrived, not the 100 that was sent.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(fotVault.previewRedeem(shares), 99e18, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_mintRevertsOnFeeOnTransferToken() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fot = new FeeOnTransferToken(100);\n        SaverVault fotVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(fot)));\n\n        fot.mint(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fot.approve(address(fotVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaverVault.AssetsNotReceived.selector, 1e18, 0.99e18)\n        );\n        fotVault.mint(1e18 * 1e6, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_reentrantTokenCannotReenterOnDeposit() public {\n        ReentrantToken hostile = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaverVault hostileVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(hostile)));\n\n        hostile.mint(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        hostile.approve(address(hostileVault), type(uint256).max);\n\n        hostile.setHook(\n            address(hostileVault), abi.encodeCall(SaverVault.deposit, (1e18, address(this)))\n        );\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(); // ReentrancyGuard\n        hostileVault.deposit(10e18, alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_reentrantTokenCannotReenterOnWithdraw() public {\n        ReentrantToken hostile = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaverVault hostileVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(hostile)));\n\n        hostile.mint(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        hostile.approve(address(hostileVault), type(uint256).max);\n        uint256 shares = hostileVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        hostile.setHook(\n            address(hostileVault), abi.encodeCall(SaverVault.redeem, (1, alice, alice))\n        );\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(); // ReentrancyGuard\n        hostileVault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_supportsTokensWithBytes32Metadata() public {\n        Bytes32MetadataToken mkr = new Bytes32MetadataToken();\n        SaverVault mkrVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(mkr)));\n\n        assertEq(mkrVault.name(), \"Saved Maker\");\n        assertEq(mkrVault.symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n        assertEq(mkrVault.decimals(), 24);\n    }\n\n    function test_supportsTokensWithNoMetadataAndNoReturnValues() public {\n        NoMetadataToken odd = new NoMetadataToken();\n        SaverVault oddVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(odd)));\n\n        assertEq(oddVault.name(), \"Saved Unknown Token\");\n        assertEq(oddVault.symbol(), \"svTKN\");\n        assertEq(oddVault.decimals(), 24); // default 18 + offset\n\n        odd.mint(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        odd.approve(address(oddVault), type(uint256).max);\n        oddVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertEq(oddVault.totalAssets(), 100e18);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Guards\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_dustDepositThatRoundsToZeroSharesReverts() public {\n        _fund(bob, 1_000e18);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e18, bob);\n\n        // Inflate the price far past the offset so a 1 wei deposit rounds down.\n        token.mint(address(vault), 1e36);\n\n        _fund(alice, 1);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaverVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(1, alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_redeemMoreThanOwnedReverts() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares + 1, alice, alice);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Factory\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_factoryIsPermissionlessAndOnePerToken() public {\n        MockERC20 other = new MockERC20(\"Other\", \"OTH\", 6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        SaverVault otherVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(other)));\n\n        assertEq(factory.vaultFor(address(other)), address(otherVault));\n        assertTrue(factory.isVault(address(otherVault)));\n        assertEq(otherVault.decimals(), 12); // 6 + offset\n\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(\n                VaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(other), address(otherVault)\n            )\n        );\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(other)));\n    }\n\n    function test_predictVaultMatchesDeployment() public {\n        MockERC20 other = new MockERC20(\"Other\", \"OTH\", 6);\n        address predicted = factory.predictVault(IERC20(address(other)));\n        assertEq(address(factory.createVault(IERC20(address(other)))), predicted);\n    }\n\n    function test_cannotListAnEOA() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(VaultFactory.TokenNotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(alice));\n assets.mulDiv(\n            supply + 10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET, _pricedAssets(supply, totalAssets_) + 1, rounding\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @dev assets = shares * (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 10**offset)\n    function _toAssets(uint256 shares, uint256 totalAssets_, Math.Rounding rounding)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        uint256 supply = totalSupply();\n        return shares.mulDiv(\n            _pricedAssets(supply, totalAssets_) + 1, supply + 10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET, rounding\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @dev While no shares exist there is nobody with a claim, so any balance\n    ///      sitting in the vault is ignored for pricing and simply accrues to\n    ///      whoever deposits first. Without this, a keeper drop (or a donation)\n    ///      into an empty vault would price the first deposit against assets it\n    ///      has no claim on and destroy most of that depositor's principal.\n    function _pricedAssets(uint256 supply, uint256 totalAssets_) private pure returns (uint256) {\n        return supply == 0 ? 0 : totalAssets_;\n    }","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {ERC20Permit} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/ERC20Permit.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC20Metadata} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Metadata.sol\";\nimport {IERC4626} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/interfaces/IERC4626.sol\";\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\nimport {Math} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol\";\n\nimport {TokenMetadata} from \"./TokenMetadata.sol\";\n\n/// @title SaverVault\n/// @notice A single-asset savings vault. Depositors get a transferable ERC-20\n///         receipt (a \"share\") representing a pro-rata claim on everything the\n///         vault holds. Yield is any increase in the vault's balance of the\n///         underlying — the keeper simply transfers tokens in.\n/// @dev Implements ERC-4626. The share price is derived from the live token\n///      balance rather than an internal counter, which is what makes a bare\n///      `transfer` from the keeper lift every holder's claim. That choice is\n///      also what makes the balance externally manipulable, so the conversion\n///      uses virtual shares/assets (see `_DECIMALS_OFFSET`) to make the\n///      first-depositor inflation attack unprofitable.\n///\n///      The underlying token is untrusted (listing is permissionless):\n///      - every transfer goes through SafeERC20, so no-return-value tokens work\n///        and a `false` return reverts;\n///      - deposits credit the *measured* balance delta, so fee-on-transfer\n///        tokens cannot mint shares against assets that never arrived;\n///      - state changes happen before external transfers and every entry point\n///        is `nonReentrant`, so tokens with transfer hooks (ERC-777 and friends)\n///        cannot re-enter mid-accounting.\ncontract SaverVault is IERC4626, ERC20, ERC20Permit, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n    using Math for uint256;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets exponent. The vault behaves as if it always\n    ///      held `10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET` extra shares backed by 1 extra wei of\n    ///      assets. This bounds the first-depositor \"donation\" attack: an\n    ///      attacker has to donate ~1e6x the victim's deposit to steal a\n    ///      meaningful fraction of it, and loses more than the victim does.\n    uint8 private constant _DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    IERC20 private immutable _ASSET;\n    uint8 private immutable _DECIMALS;\n\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error ZeroAssets();\n    error AssetsNotReceived(uint256 expected, uint256 received);\n    error ExceedsMaxWithdraw(uint256 requested, uint256 max);\n    error ExceedsMaxRedeem(uint256 requested, uint256 max);\n\n    /// @param asset_ The underlying ERC-20 this vault saves.\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_)\n        ERC20(name_, symbol_)\n        ERC20Permit(name_)\n    {\n        _ASSET = asset_;\n        _DECIMALS = TokenMetadata.decimalsOf(address(asset_)) + _DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Metadata\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @dev Underlying decimals plus the virtual offset, so that share amounts\n    ///      keep the same order of magnitude as asset amounts in a UI.\n    function decimals() public view override(ERC20, IERC20Metadata) returns (uint8) {\n        return _DECIMALS;\n    }\n\n    function asset() public view returns (address) {\n        return address(_ASSET);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Everything the vault can pay out: deposits plus all yield the\n    ///         keeper has sent in, minus anything already withdrawn.\n    function totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _ASSET.balanceOf(address(this));\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Conversion\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function convertToShares(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toShares(assets, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    function convertToAssets(uint256 shares) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toAssets(shares, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev shares = assets * (totalSupply + 10**offset) / (totalAssets + 1)\n    function _toShares(uint256 assets, uint256 totalAssets_, Math.Rounding rounding)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        return assets.mulDiv(totalSupply() + 10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssets_ + 1, rounding);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev assets = shares * (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 10**offset)\n    function _toAssets(uint256 shares, uint256 totalAssets_, Math.Rounding rounding)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        return shares.mulDiv(totalAssets_ + 1, totalSupply() + 10 ** _DECIMALS_OFFSET, rounding);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Limits\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function maxDeposit(address) public pure returns (uint256) {\n        return type(uint256).max;\n    }\n\n    function maxMint(address) public pure returns (uint256) {\n        return type(uint256).max;\n    }\n\n    function maxWithdraw(address owner) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return convertToAssets(balanceOf(owner));\n    }\n\n    function maxRedeem(address owner) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return balanceOf(owner);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Previews\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Rounding always favours the vault (i.e. the existing holders), so no\n    // sequence of deposits/withdrawals can round value out of the vault.\n\n    function previewDeposit(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toShares(assets, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    function previewMint(uint256 shares) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toAssets(shares, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n    }\n\n    function previewWithdraw(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toShares(assets, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n    }\n\n    function previewRedeem(uint256 shares) public view returns (uint256) {\n        return _toAssets(shares, totalAssets(), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Entry points\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Deposit `assets` of the underlying and receive shares.\n    /// @dev Shares are priced off the balance *before* the transfer and minted\n    ///      against the amount that actually arrived, so a fee-on-transfer\n    ///      token credits only what the vault really received.\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver)\n        public\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        uint256 totalAssetsBefore = totalAssets();\n        uint256 received = new MockERC20(\"Dai Stablecoin\", \"DAI\", 18);\n        vault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(token)));\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n Core accounting\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrips() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 100e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        // Virtual assets make the vault keep at most 1 wei of dust.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(assets, 100e18, 1);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_keeperYieldLiftsEveryHolderProRata() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        _fund(bob, 300e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(300e18, bob);\n\n        // Keeper just transfers yield in. No vault call at all.\n        token.mint(keeper, 40e18);\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 40e18);\n\n        // 10% return each, split 1:3.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 110e18, 1e6);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 330e18, 1e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 440e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_sharesAreTransferableAndCarryTheClaim() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 0);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 100e18, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(token.balanceOf(bob), 100e18, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawViaAllowance() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, type(uint256).max);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.withdraw(40e18, bob, alice);\n\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(bob), 40e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawWithoutAllowanceReverts() public {\n        _fund(alice, 100e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.withdraw(40e18, bob, alice);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // the share price, then let a victim deposit and round to zero.\n    /// The virtual offset makes it a loss for the attacker, not a profit.\n    function test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _fund(attacker, 10_000e18 + 1);\n        _fund(alice, 10_000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n        token.transfer(address(vault), 10_000e18); // donation\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceShares = vault.deposit(10_000e18, alice);\n        assertGt(aliceShares, 0, \"victim must not round to zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceOut = vault.redeem(aliceShares, alice, alice);\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n fotVault.mint(1e18 * 1e6, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_reentrantTokenCannotReenterOnDeposit() public {\n        ReentrantToken hostile = new ReentrantToken();\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTjcQTgfEQMbYpGdNkk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01BiM8ni2XD5fENFVHGmtNZG","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122518Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/NOTES.md","content":"# Saver vaults — implementation notes\n\n## What's here\n\n| File | Role |\n| --- | --- |\n| `src/SaverVault.sol` | One vault per underlying ERC-20. ERC-4626. The receipt token is the vault itself (transferable, `permit`-enabled). |\n| `src/VaultFactory.sol` | Permissionless listing. One canonical vault per token, CREATE2 so the address is predictable. Holds no funds, no owner, no upgrade path. |\n| `src/TokenMetadata.sol` | Best-effort `name`/`symbol`/`decimals` reads that survive non-conforming tokens. |\n| `script/Deploy.s.sol` | Deploys the factory. That's the whole deployment — vaults come later, from anyone. |\n\n`forge build` compiles; `forge test` runs 20 tests covering the accounting, the\nmanipulation cases, and the hostile-token cases below.\n\nThere are no admin roles anywhere. Nobody can pause a vault, upgrade it, change\na fee, or move a depositor's assets. The tradeoff is that nothing can be fixed\nafter the fact either — see *Accepted limitations*.\n\n---\n\n## How a depositor's claim is computed\n\nA vault holds one balance and issues shares against it. A share is a claim on a\nfraction of **everything the vault holds right now**:\n\n```\ntotalAssets() = underlying.balanceOf(vault)\n```\n\nThat single line is what makes the keeper work. The keeper does a plain\n`transfer` into the vault — no vault call, no allowance, no role. The balance\ngoes up, `totalAssets()` goes up, and every existing share is worth more. No\nper-user bookkeeping, no distribution loop.\n\n### The conversion\n\nWith `S = totalSupply()` (shares), `A = totalAssets()`, and a fixed\n`OFFSET = 6`:\n\n```\nshares_out = assets_in * (S + 10^OFFSET) / (A + 1)     // deposit,  rounded down\nassets_out = shares_in * (A + 1) / (S + 10^OFFSET)     // redeem,   rounded down\n```\n\nThe `+ 10^OFFSET` and `+ 1` are *virtual* shares and assets — the vault prices\nas if it permanently held 1e6 extra shares backed by 1 extra wei. They are never\nminted and never redeemable. Their job is explained under *Share-price\nmanipulation*.\n\nRounding always favours the vault, i.e. the existing holders: shares out of a\ndeposit round **down**, shares burned for a withdrawal round **up**. A depositor\ncan lose at most 1 wei to rounding; no sequence of deposits and withdrawals can\nround value *out* of the vault (`test_roundTripChurnCannotDrainOtherHolders`).\n\n### Worked example\n\n| Step | S (shares) | A (assets) | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Alice deposits 100 DAI | 0 → 100e24 | 0 → 100e18 | `100e18 * (0 + 1e6) / (0 + 1)` = 100e24 shares |\n| Bob deposits 300 DAI | → 400e24 | → 400e18 | `300e18 * (100e24 + 1e6) / (100e18 + 1)` = 300e24 shares |\n| Keeper transfers 40 DAI | 400e24 | → 440e18 | no shares minted — everyone's claim rises 10% |\n| Alice redeems all | → 300e24 | → 330e18 | `100e24 * (440e18 + 1) / (400e24 + 1e6)` = 110 DAI |\n\nAlice deposited 100 and withdrew 110; Bob's remaining 300e24 shares are now worth\n330. Share counts are 1e6× the asset amounts because of the offset — that's also\nwhy `vault.decimals()` is `underlying.decimals() + 6`.\n\n### Deposits credit what actually arrived\n\n`deposit()` snapshots the balance, pulls the tokens, and mints against the\n**measured delta**, not the requested amount. A fee-on-transfer token that\ndelivers 99 of a requested 100 mints shares for 99. Crediting the requested\namount would mint claims against assets that were never received, which every\nother holder pays for.\n\n`mint()` (exact shares out) can't do that — honouring \"exactly N shares\" against\na short delivery is the bug we just avoided — so it reverts with\n`AssetsNotReceived` on fee-on-transfer tokens. Front-ends should route those\ntokens to `deposit()`.\n\n### Empty vaults\n\nWhile `totalSupply() == 0` nobody holds a claim, so any balance already sitting\nin the vault is ignored for pricing and accrues to whoever deposits first.\nWithout that branch, a keeper transfer that lands before the first deposit would\nprice that deposit against assets it has no claim on and destroy most of its\nprincipal.\n\n---\n\n## Share-price manipulation\n\n`totalAssets()` reads a live balance, so *anyone* can raise it by sending tokens\nin. That is the feature (it's how yield arrives); it also means the classic\nfirst-depositor inflation attack applies. The virtual offset is the defence.\n\nThe attack: deposit 1 wei, donate a large amount to push the price above one\nwhole share, let a victim deposit, and their share count rounds to zero — you\nown 100% of their money. With `OFFSET = 6` the attacker's 1 wei buys 1e6 shares,\nbut the vault also prices against 1e6 virtual shares it doesn't own, so the\ndonation is split with the virtual holder rather than captured. Running the\nnumbers (`test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable`): attacker seeds 1 wei, donates\n10,000, victim deposits 10,000 → victim redeems ~10,000 (whole), attacker\nredeems ~5,000 of the 10,000 they spent. The attack is a guaranteed loss, and\ngets worse the harder it's pushed.\n\nTwo smaller guards back it up:\n\n- a deposit that would mint zero shares reverts (`ZeroShares`) instead of taking\n  the money silently;\n- there is no need to seed a vault at listing time, though doing so is still\n  good hygiene.\n\n---\n\n## Operating a vault\n\n### Listing a token\n\nListing is permissionless and the contracts trust the token for nothing except\nvalue. Everything below is a property of the *token*, and the vault inherits it\nwhole — screening is the operator's job, not the contract's.\n\n**Handled by the contracts:**\n\n| Token behaviour | What happens |\n| --- | --- |\n| No return value on `transfer` (USDT) | Fine — SafeERC20. |\n| Returns `false` instead of reverting | Reverts. |\n| `bytes32` `name`/`symbol` (MKR) | Fine — falls back to unpacking. |\n| Missing `decimals()`/`symbol()` | Defaults to 18 / `TKN`. |\n| Fee-on-transfer | `deposit` credits the delta; `mint` reverts. |\n| Transfer hooks / ERC-777 | `nonReentrant` on all four entry points, state written before any transfer out. |\n| Reverts on zero-value transfer | Never reached — zero-share/zero-asset calls revert first. |\n| Rebasing (stETH, aTokens) | Positive rebase reads as yield. Negative rebase is a pro-rata loss to all holders. Quotes go stale between blocks. |\n\n**Not handled — decide before you list:**\n\n- **Pausable or blacklistable tokens** (USDC, USDT). The issuer can freeze the\n  vault's address. Deposits and withdrawals both stop and there is no\n  administrative escape hatch. This is unfixable onchain; it's a disclosure, not\n  a bug.\n- **Upgradeable tokens.** The token's admin can mint, seize, or change transfer\n  semantics at any time. The vault is exactly as trustworthy as the token.\n- **Tokens with a broken or lying `balanceOf`.** Share price is derived from it.\n  A malicious implementation is a total loss.\n- **Name and symbol are attacker-controlled strings.** Anyone can list a token\n  called \"USD Coin\" with symbol \"USDC\", and anyone can deploy a `SaverVault`\n  directly without going through the factory. Front-ends and integrators must\n  key on the **underlying token address** and check `factory.isVault(vault)` /\n  `factory.vaultFor(token)`. Never resolve a vault by displayed name.\n- **Low-liquidity or unlisted tokens.** A vault is not an endorsement. The\n  product surface should say so.\n\n### Running the keeper\n\nThe keeper is just an EOA (or bot) that transfers the underlying to the vault\naddress. There is no keeper role in the contracts, so a leaked keeper key\nexposes only the keeper's own funds — not the vault's.\n\n1. **Yield drops are sandwichable. This is the biggest operational risk.**\n   Withdrawals are open, there is no lockup, and a drop lands in a single block.\n   A searcher who sees the keeper transaction in the mempool can deposit in\n   front of it and withdraw immediately behind it, capturing a share of the drop\n   proportional to the size of their deposit while taking no risk. On a 400-DAI\n   vault, a 40-DAI drop is +10% instantly; a searcher depositing 10,000 DAI in\n   front takes ~96% of it, and the actual savers get the crumbs.\n\n   Mitigations, in order of how much they cost you:\n   - **Submit privately.** Send the drop as a Flashbots/MEV-Share bundle so it\n     never sits in the public mempool. This is the minimum bar and should be\n     considered mandatory on mainnet.\n   - **Drip more often, smaller.** Per-drop profit below the searcher's gas plus\n     risk makes it not worth attacking. Cheap, partial.\n   - **Vest the yield** if a vault grows large enough to be worth attacking\n     properly. Add a `report()` that recognises the newly-arrived balance and\n     releases it linearly over a few hours, with\n     `totalAssets() = balance - lockedProfit`. This is a real change to the\n     accounting above and needs its own review; it's the only structural fix,\n     because private submission still leaks the drop the moment it's mined.\n\n   As specified — open withdrawals, no fee, lump transfers — this cannot be\n   fixed from the keeper side alone. Flagging it as a design decision to make\n   deliberately rather than a bug to file.\n\n2. **Never drop into a vault with `totalSupply() == 0`.** The first depositor\n   would take the whole thing (see *Empty vaults*). Nobody loses principal, but\n   you've given the money away. Check supply before sending.\n\n3. **Send the underlying and only the underlying.** There is no sweep or rescue\n   function — deliberately, since any sweep is a lever on vault assets and this\n   design has no one trustworthy to hold it. Tokens sent to the wrong vault, and\n   any non-underlying token sent to a vault, are unrecoverable. Verify the vault\n   address against `factory.vaultFor(token)` on every send.\n\n4. **Retries are safe.** A duplicated drop is just more yield. There is no\n   sequence number, no idempotency key, and nothing that can be double-counted.\n\n5. **Monitor** `totalAssets()` against `totalSupply()`. Share price should be\n   monotonically non-decreasing except where the token itself loses value\n   (negative rebase, fee-on-transfer withdrawals).
