ERC-4626. The receipt token is the vault itself (transferable, `permit`-enabled). |\n| `src/VaultFactory.sol` | Permissionless listing. One canonical vault per token, CREATE2 so the address is predictable. Holds no funds, no owner, no upgrade path. |\n| `src/TokenMetadata.sol` | Best-effort `name`/`symbol`/`decimals` reads that survive non-conforming tokens. |\n| `script/Deploy.s.sol` | Deploys the factory. That's the whole deployment — vaults come later, from anyone. |\n\n`forge build` compiles; `forge test` runs 20 tests covering the accounting, the\nmanipulation cases, and the hostile-token cases below.\n\nThere are no admin roles anywhere. Nobody can pause a vault, upgrade it, change\na fee, or move a depositor's assets. The tradeoff is that nothing can be fixed\nafter the fact either — see *Accepted limitations*.\n\n---\n\n## How a depositor's claim is computed\n\nA vault holds one balance and issues shares against it. A share is a claim on a\nfraction of **everything the vault holds right now**:\n\n```\ntotalAssets() = underlying.balanceOf(vault)\n```\n\nThat single line is what makes the keeper work. The keeper does a plain\n`transfer` into the vault — no vault call, no allowance, no role. The balance\ngoes up, `totalAssets()` goes up, and every existing share is worth more. No\nper-user bookkeeping, no distribution loop.\n\n### The conversion\n\nWith `S = totalSupply()` (shares), `A = totalAssets()`, and a fixed\n`OFFSET = 6`:\n\n```\nshares_out = assets_in * (S + 10^OFFSET) / (A + 1)     // deposit,  rounded down\nassets_out = shares_in * (A + 1) / (S + 10^OFFSET)     // redeem,   rounded down\n```\n\nThe `+ 10^OFFSET` and `+ 1` are *virtual* shares and assets — the vault prices\nas if it permanently held 1e6 extra shares backed by 1 extra wei. They are never\nminted and never redeemable. Their job is explained under *Share-price\nmanipulation*.\n\nRounding always favours the vault, i.e. the existing holders: shares out of a\ndeposit round **down**, shares burned for a withdrawal round **up**. A depositor\ncan lose at most 1 wei to rounding; no sequence of deposits and withdrawals can\nround value *out* of the vault (`test_roundTripChurnCannotDrainOtherHolders`).\n\n### Worked example\n\n| Step | S (shares) | A (assets) | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Alice deposits 100 DAI | 0 → 100e24 | 0 → 100e18 | `100e18 * (0 + 1e6) / (0 + 1)` = 100e24 shares |\n| Bob deposits 300 DAI | → 400e24 | → 400e18 | `300e18 * (100e24 + 1e6) / (100e18 + 1)` = 300e24 shares |\n| Keeper transfers 40 DAI | 400e24 | → 440e18 | no shares minted — everyone's claim rises 10% |\n| Alice redeems all | → 300e24 | → 330e18 | `100e24 * (440e18 + 1) / (400e24 + 1e6)` = 110 DAI |\n\nAlice deposited 100 and withdrew 110; Bob's remaining 300e24 shares are now worth\n330. Share counts are 1e6× the asset amounts because of the offset — that's also\nwhy `vault.decimals()` is `underlying.decimals() + 6`.\n\n### Deposits credit what actually arrived\n\n`deposit()` snapshots the balance, pulls the tokens, and mints against the\n**measured delta**, not the requested amount. A fee-on-transfer token that\ndelivers 99 of a requested 100 mints shares for 99. Crediting the requested\namount would mint claims against assets that were never received, which every\nother holder pays for.\n\n`mint()` (exact shares out) can't do that — honouring \"exactly N shares\" against\na short delivery is the bug we just avoided — so it reverts with\n`AssetsNotReceived` on fee-on-transfer tokens. Front-ends should route those\ntokens to `deposit()`.\n\n### Empty vaults\n\nWhile `totalSupply() == 0` nobody holds a claim, so any balance already sitting\nin the vault is ignored for pricing and accrues to whoever deposits first.\nWithout that branch, a keeper transfer that lands before the first deposit would\nprice that deposit against assets it has no claim on and destroy most of its\nprincipal.\n\n---\n\n## Share-price manipulation\n\n`totalAssets()` reads a live balance, so *anyone* can raise it by sending tokens\nin. That is the feature (it's how yield arrives); it also means the classic\nfirst-depositor inflation attack applies. The virtual offset is the defence.\n\nThe attack: deposit 1 wei, donate a large amount to push the price above one\nwhole share, let a victim deposit, and their share count rounds to zero — you\nown 100% of their money. With `OFFSET = 6` the attacker's 1 wei buys 1e6 shares,\nbut the vault also prices against 1e6 virtual shares it doesn't own, so the\ndonation is split with the virtual holder rather than captured. Running the\nnumbers (`test_inflationAttackIsUnprofitable`): attacker seeds 1 wei, donates\n10,000, victim deposits 10,000 → victim redeems ~10,000 (whole), attacker\nredeems ~5,000 of the 10,000 they spent. The attack is a guaranteed loss, and\ngets worse the harder it's pushed.\n\nTwo smaller guards back it up:\n\n- a deposit that would mint zero shares reverts (`ZeroShares`) instead of taking\n  the money silently;\n- there is no need to seed a vault at listing time, though doing so is still\n  good hygiene.\n\n---\n\n## Operating a vault\n\n### Listing a token\n\nListing is permissionless and the contracts trust the token for nothing except\nvalue. Everything below is a property of the *token*, and the vault inherits it\nwhole — screening is the operator's job, not the contract's.\n\n**Handled by the contracts:**\n\n| Token behaviour | What happens |\n| --- | --- |\n| No return value on `transfer` (USDT) | Fine — SafeERC20. |\n| Returns `false` instead of reverting | Reverts. |\n| `bytes32` `name`/`symbol` (MKR) | Fine — falls back to unpacking. |\n| Missing `decimals()`/`symbol()` | Defaults to 18 / `TKN`. |\n| Fee-on-transfer | `deposit` credits the delta; `mint` reverts. |\n| Transfer hooks / ERC-777 | `nonReentrant` on all four entry points, state written before any transfer out. |\n| Reverts on zero-value transfer | Never reached — zero-share/zero-asset calls revert first. |\n| Rebasing (stETH, aTokens) | Positive rebase reads as yield. Negative rebase is a pro-rata loss to all holders. Quotes go stale between blocks. |\n\n**Not handled — decide before you list:**\n\n- **Pausable or blacklistable tokens** (USDC, USDT). The issuer can freeze the\n  vault's address. Deposits and withdrawals both stop and there is no\n  administrative escape hatch. This is unfixable onchain; it's a disclosure, not\n  a bug.\n- **Upgradeable tokens.** The token's admin can mint, seize, or change transfer\n  semantics at any time. The vault is exactly as trustworthy as the token.\n- **Tokens with a broken or lying `balanceOf`.** Share price is derived from it.\n  A malicious implementation is a total loss.\n- **Name and symbol are attacker-controlled strings.** Anyone can list a token\n  called \"USD Coin\" with symbol \"USDC\", and anyone can deploy a `SaverVault`\n  directly without going through the factory. Front-ends and integrators must\n  key on the **underlying token address** and check `factory.isVault(vault)` /\n  `factory.vaultFor(token)`. Never resolve a vault by displayed name.\n- **Low-liquidity or unlisted tokens.** A vault is not an endorsement. The\n  product surface should say so.\n\n### Running the keeper\n\nThe keeper is just an EOA (or bot) that transfers the underlying to the vault\naddress. There is no keeper role in the contracts, so a leaked keeper key\nexposes only the keeper's own funds — not the vault's.\n\n1. **Yield drops are sandwichable. This is the biggest operational risk.**\n   Withdrawals are open, there is no lockup, and a drop lands in a single block.\n   A searcher who sees the keeper transaction in the mempool can deposit in\n   front of it and withdraw immediately behind it, capturing a share of the drop\n   proportional to the size of their deposit while taking no risk. On a 400-DAI\n   vault, a 40-DAI drop is +10% instantly; a searcher depositing 10,000 DAI in\n   front takes ~96% of it, and the actual savers get the crumbs.\n\n   Mitigations, in order of how much they cost you:\n   - **Submit privately.** Send the drop as a Flashbots/MEV-Share bundle so it\n     never sits in the public mempool. This is the minimum bar and should be\n     considered mandatory on mainnet.\n   - **Drip more often, smaller.** Per-drop profit below the searcher's gas plus\n     risk makes it not worth attacking. Cheap, partial.\n   - **Vest the yield** if a vault grows large enough to be worth attacking\n     properly. Add a `report()` that recognises the newly-arrived balance and\n     releases it linearly over a few hours, with\n     `totalAssets() = balance - lockedProfit`. This is a real change to the\n     accounting above and needs its own review; it's the only structural fix,\n     because private submission still leaks the drop the moment it's mined.\n\n   As specified — open withdrawals, no fee, lump transfers — this cannot be\n   fixed from the keeper side alone. Flagging it as a design decision to make\n   deliberately rather than a bug to file.\n\n2. **Never drop into a vault with `totalSupply() == 0`.** The first depositor\n   would take the whole thing (see *Empty vaults*). Nobody loses principal, but\n   you've given the money away. Check supply before sending.\n\n3. **Send the underlying and only the underlying.** There is no sweep or rescue\n   function — deliberately, since any sweep is a lever on vault assets and this\n   design has no one trustworthy to hold it. Tokens sent to the wrong vault, and\n   any non-underlying token sent to a vault, are unrecoverable. Verify the vault\n   address against `factory.vaultFor(token)` on every send.\n\n4. **Retries are safe.** A duplicated drop is just more yield. There is no\n   sequence number, no idempotency key, and nothing that can be double-counted.\n\n5. **Monitor** `totalAssets()` against `totalSupply()`. Share price should be\n   monotonically non-decreasing except where the token itself loses value\n   (negative rebase, fee-on-transfer withdrawals). A drop in share price without\n   one of those is a token-level incident.\n\n---\n\n## Accepted limitations\n\n- **No pause, no upgrade, no admin.** A bug ships permanently. This is the right\n  trade for a permissionless listing product — an admin key over every vault of\n  every token is a bigger target than the bug it would fix — but it means the\n  code needs an audit before mainnet, not after.\n- **No fees.** Nothing in the contracts takes a cut. Adding one later means a new\n  factory and a migration, not an upgrade.\n- **Read-only reentrancy.** A token with transfer hooks can hand control to a\n  third party mid-`deposit`/`redeem`. Vault state is self-consistent at those\n  points, but integrators quoting `convertToAssets` from inside such a callback\n  should apply the usual care.\n- **`mint()` is unusable for fee-on-transfer tokens** by design. `deposit()`\n  covers them.\n- **A token with malformed ABI-encoded string metadata** can make its own\n  `createVault` call revert. It affects only that token's listing.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Everything builds and all 20 tests pass.\n\n## What's in the directory\n\n```\nsrc/SaverVault.sol      ERC-4626 vault; the receipt token is the vault itself (transferable, permit)\nsrc/VaultFactory.sol    permissionless listing, one canonical vault per token, CREATE2\nsrc/TokenMetadata.sol   metadata reads that survive non-conforming tokens\nscript/Deploy.s.sol     deploys the factory (that's the whole deployment)\ntest/                   20 tests: accounting, manipulation, hostile tokens\nNOTES.md                claim math + operator guide\n```\n\n## Key design points\n\n**Claim math.** `totalAssets() = underlying.balanceOf(vault)` — that's what makes the keeper's bare `transfer` lift every holder's claim with no bookkeeping. Shares convert with virtual shares/assets (`+1e6` shares, `+1` wei), rounding always toward the vault.\n\n**Because the price reads a live balance, anyone can move it.** That's the feature and the vulnerability. The virtual offset makes the first-depositor inflation attack a guaranteed loss for the attacker (test: attacker seeds 1 wei + donates 10k, victim redeems ~whole, attacker recovers ~half of what they spent).\n\n**Permissionless listing means the token is untrusted.** Deposits credit the measured balance delta, so fee-on-transfer tokens can't mint claims against assets that never arrived; `mint()` (exact-shares) reverts on those rather than fake it. All four entry points are `nonReentrant` with state written before transfers out, for tokens with hooks. SafeERC20 throughout. bytes32 metadata (MKR) and missing metadata both work.\n\n**One guard I added beyond the brief:** a keeper drop landing before the first deposit would otherwise price that deposit against assets it has no claim on and destroy most of its principal. While `totalSupply() == 0` the existing balance is ignored for pricing and accrues to the first depositor.\n\n## One thing to decide deliberately\n\nOpen withdrawals + no lockup + lump yield transfers means **yield drops are sandwichable**. A searcher who sees the keeper tx in the mempool deposits in front and withdraws behind, taking a share proportional to their deposit at zero risk — on a 400-token vault, a 40-token drop lets a 10k deposit take ~96% of it. This is inherent to the mechanism as specified, not a contract bug, so I built it as asked and documented it as the top operator item: private submission (Flashbots) is the minimum bar, smaller/more frequent drips help, and linear profit vesting via a `report()` is the only structural fix — that one changes the accounting and would need its own review. Say the word if you want me to build the vesting variant.\n\nOther operator items in NOTES.md: pausable/blacklistable tokens can freeze a vault with no escape hatch (there is no admin anywhere, by design), token names/symbols are attacker-controlled so UIs must key on `factory.isVault` and the underlying address, and there's no sweep function — wrong-token sends are unrecoverable."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9858,"cache_read_input_tokens":74951,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9858},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"549bf3c0-fae5-443d-8cc7-81022d8a8770","uuid":"1c027367-e92c-4d0b-9449-b8d8dabe80d8","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:35:15.365Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTsoMFaCLea1WPkTHzx"}
